<thought>The 13C NMR shows a single distinct upfield carbon at ~19 ppm, which is typical for a methyl carbon. In cases where two methyl groups are chemically equivalent (e.g., the two methyls of an isopropyl group), they give one carbon signal but represent two CH₃ groups. To confirm the count, I will retrieve the HSQC spectrum, which correlates each carbon with its attached protons. By checking how many proton signals are attached to the ~19 ppm carbon, I can determine whether there are one or two methyl groups.</thought>
